conflicts.subject: model
conflicts.detail: Authorization models differ (A: no authentication or authorization; every endpoint is open (the documented gateway auth does not exist in the code); B: none: a local library with no users)
solutions: Choose one authorization model and express the others' rules in it
conflicts.recommended: One authorization model with one permission check function

resolution.decision: Owner-only model: every Book, Rating, ReadingList and list entry belongs to one person (owner_id); every read and write checks owner_id against the signed-in person in one permission function; another person's ids answer 404. No roles. Neither source had any authorization (Shelfie's documented gateway auth does not exist in its code); this is needed because the user wants 'people' to keep libraries. Alternative not chosen: a single-person local app with no accounts.
resolution.note: pre-approved recommendation (benchmark operator); no live user

conflicts.subject: session
conflicts.detail: Session mechanisms differ (A: none in use: shelfie_session_secret is required at startup but never used; B: none)
solutions: Choose one session mechanism (http-only cookie sessions are the safer default for web apps)
Use tokens only where a client cannot hold cookies
conflicts.recommended: One session mechanism for the whole app

resolution.decision: Email and password sign-in (password hashed with the standard library's scrypt), server-side session stored in the database, random token in an http-only, SameSite=Lax cookie; sign out deletes the session. Shelfie's unused SHELFIE_SESSION_SECRET is not carried over.

conflicts.subject: existing-data-import
conflicts.detail: Both apps key books with their own integer ids in separate SQLite files (shelfie.db, readr.db). Importing both into one database would collide on ids and require re-keying Readr's books and rewriting its ratings and list_books rows; there is also no user to own imported rows. No database files were provided and nothing shows whether real data exists.
solutions: Start the unified app with an empty database; import is out of scope for now
Write an import that re-keys Readr's ids into the unified Book table and assigns all rows to one chosen person (destructive-risk migration needing its own plan and approval)
conflicts.recommended: Start empty; if the user has data worth keeping, plan the import separately with templates/migration-plan.md, a backup and a dry run

resolution.decision: Start the unified app with an empty database; no import of shelfie.db or readr.db in this plan (none was provided; whether real data exists is unknown). If the user has data, an import that re-keys Readr's ids is planned separately with templates/migration-plan.md, a backup and a dry run, and needs its own migration approval.
resolution.note: plan approved; any future import needs its own approval

conflicts.subject: book
conflicts.detail: Book may not mean the same thing in A, B: A describes it as 'A book in the library (Shelfie's catalog).', B as 'A book that can be rated or listed (title only).'
solutions: Keep them as separate entities with distinct names (for example UserAccount and LedgerAccount)
Merge them only if the user confirms they describe the same thing
conflicts.recommended: Ask the user; never merge entities because their names match

resolution.decision: Same thing: both are a 'books' table with integer id and required title, referenced the same way by ratings (and by Readr's list_books). Merge into one Book (id, owner_id, title required, author optional). Field origins listed in architecture.json.
resolution.note: pre-approved recommendation (benchmark operator); evidence A-E01, B-E03

conflicts.subject: export-format
conflicts.detail: Shelfie's README and spec promise CSV at /api/v1/books/export.csv; the code returns JSON at /api/books/export (A-C01, A-C02).
solutions: JSON as the code does
CSV as the docs claim (new work, not in any source's behaviour)
both
conflicts.recommended: JSON only; CSV listed as a possible later addition if the user wants it

resolution.decision: JSON export only ([{title, stars}] for the signed-in person's books); no CSV.

conflicts.subject: rating-cardinality
conflicts.detail: Both apps append a new ratings row each time a book is rated, so a book collects several ratings and Shelfie's export repeats it. A shared, multi-person app needs a clear rule.
solutions: One rating per person per book; rating again replaces it
Keep every rating as history and show the latest or the average
conflicts.recommended: One rating per person per book (unique key, upsert); history is not in the user's request

resolution.decision: One rating per person per book (unique (owner, book)); rating again replaces it; a rating can be cleared.

conflicts.subject: rating-scale
conflicts.detail: Shelfie's README and OpenAPI spec say ratings are 1-10 in a field called 'score'; Shelfie's code and Readr's code both use 1-5 'stars'. Documentation vs code, not code vs code (A-C03, A-C04).
solutions: 1-5 stars as both apps' code does
1-10 as Shelfie's old docs say (would need a conversion and a decision from the user)
conflicts.recommended: 1-5 integer stars: what both apps actually do, and the user said to trust the code

resolution.decision: Integer 1-5 'stars', enforced on the server and by a database CHECK; anything else is 400. The 1-10 'score' scale in Shelfie's old docs is not used.

conflicts.subject: write-persistence
conflicts.detail: Neither source ever commits a transaction, so (inferred from sqlite3 defaults; not run) writes would be lost when the process exits; neither enables SQLite foreign keys, so ratings and list entries can point at missing books.
solutions: Commit every write and turn on PRAGMA foreign_keys in the unified app
Copy the sources' behaviour
conflicts.recommended: Commit every write, enable foreign keys, and test that data survives a restart

resolution.decision: Commit every write; PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON on every connection; deleting a book removes its rating and list entries (cascade); data survives a restart.

conflicts.subject: book
conflicts.detail: Book exists in A:Book, B:Book; fields not shared: author (only A)
solutions: Merge into one table holding the fields kept features need
Keep separate tables if the two only share a name, and rename one
conflicts.recommended: Merge only once it is confirmed they mean the same thing; then list every field's origin in architecture.json

resolution.decision: Merge into one Book table holding title (A, B) and author (A only, nullable).

conflicts.subject: path-version-prefix
conflicts.detail: Shelfie's spec uses /api/v1/...; its code serves /api/... (A-C05). Readr has no API.
solutions: Use /api/... as the code does
Adopt /api/v1/... for the new app
conflicts.recommended: Use /api/... (the observed shape); versioning is not needed for a new single app

resolution.decision: Use /api/... without a version prefix, as Shelfie's code does.
